guard: bypassable: escapeContent() (src/utils/scriptExecution.ts:335-340) only escapes backslash, backtick and $ -- it never escapes a literal double-quote or newline, even though the value is placed inside a double-quoted JS string. A perspectiveName such as `x", (function(){ ATTACKER_CODE(); })()); //` closes the string early and runs an arbitrary trailing IIFE as part of the OmniJS script OmniFocus evaluates.
why: perspectiveName is caller-controlled per its own zod schema (z.string(), no restriction, see src/tools/definitions/getPerspectiveView.ts:6). I traced it from the handler through getPerspectiveView() into executeOmniFocusScript(scriptPath, [perspectiveName, limit.toString()]) in scriptExecution.ts, where args are quoted with escapeContent and joined into `const argv = [...]`. Unlike queryOmnifocus.ts's escapeJXA (which does escape quotes), escapeContent does not, so a perspectiveName containing a double quote breaks out of the string and injects arbitrary OmniJS that runs inside OmniFocus's automation engine with the same privileges as the rest of the script -- turning a nominally read-only 'get this perspective' tool into arbitrary code execution against the whole database (create/delete/modify any task or project, and Omni Automation's networking APIs such as URL.fetch could exfiltrate data), which is a genuine confidentiality/integrity violation beyond the tool's declared contract.

sink: spliced verbatim (zero escaping) as a raw JS property-access expression inside the generated JXA sort comparator (generateSortLogic), which is written to a temp file and executed via osascript -l JavaScript
why: sortBy is caller-controlled per its own zod schema (z.string().optional(), no enum -- src/tools/definitions/queryOmnifocus.ts:46), described only informally as accepting field names like 'name, dueDate, ...' but nothing in code enforces that. Every other filter value in this same file (projectName, taskName, tags, status, etc.) is passed through the file's own escapeJXA() helper before interpolation, but generateSortLogic() (line 671-694) interpolates sortBy directly into `a.${sortBy}`/`b.${sortBy}` with no quoting and no escaping at all -- it is not even inside a string literal, so no quote-escaping would be needed to defend it; any value works as raw code. A sortBy of `x = (function(){ /* attacker OmniJS runs here */ return 0; })()` produces `let aVal = a.x = (function(){ ... })();`, which is syntactically valid and executes the attacker's IIFE with full access to the OmniFocus document model on every element compared during Array.prototype.sort -- turning the declared read-only query tool into arbitrary code execution (can create/delete/modify any task or project, and Omni Automation networking APIs could exfiltrate data). The `fields` array (z.array(z.string())) has an independent, equally unescaped fallback sink at generateFieldMapping() line 850 (`${field}: item.${field} !== undefined ? item.${field} : null`) for the same root cause -- no escapeJXA applied -- though it is harder to craft a single clean field value across all three raw substitutions there, so sortBy is the clearer, directly provable bypass.
